STUDYQURAN:2:204/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r1.speaker: IK, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r1.claim: Most cited commentators prefer to read 2:204–7 as universal teaching on hypocrisy, despite reports of specific incidents.
STUDYQURAN:2:204/r1.anchor: most prefer to see these verses as universal teachings on the nature of hypocrisy (IK, R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:2:206/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:206/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:206/r1.claim: Sufficiency is used positively and negatively in the Quran, often to mean serving something’s purpose.
STUDYQURAN:2:206/r1.anchor: negative sense in the Quran, often in the sense of “serving the purpose” of

STUDYQURAN:2:206/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:206/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:206/r2.claim: Here Hell serves to punish the misdeeds of the person who works corruption.
STUDYQURAN:2:206/r2.anchor: in this case punishing the misdeeds of the worker of corruption

TAB-FULL:v3p572/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that hypocrites mocked the Muslims killed at al-Rajīʿ as having died pointlessly; the verses contrast their hypocrisy and corruption with the martyrs’ reward and those who give themselves for God.
TAB-FULL:v3p572/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال " لما أصيبت هذه السرية أصحاب خبيب بالرجيع بين مكة، والمدينة، فقال رجال من المنافقين

TAB-FULL:v3p588/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r1.claim: When the hypocrite is urged to fear God and stop corrupting land and destroying Muslim crops and offspring, he grows arrogantly proud through sin and persists in error; Hell is sufficient punishment.
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r1.anchor: استكبر ودخلته عزة، وحمية بما حرم الله عليه، وتمادى في غيه وضلاله

TAB-FULL:v3p588/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r2.claim: Hell is a sufficient punishment for his transgression, and a wretched bed for those consigned to it.
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r2.anchor: فكفاه عقوبة من غيه وضلاله صلي نار جهنم ولبئس المهاد لصاليها

TAB-FULL:v3p588/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r3.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r3.claim: Some interpreters take the person described as any sinner and hypocrite.
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r3.anchor: فقال بعضهم: عنى بها كل فاسق، ومنافق

TAB-FULL:v3p588/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r4.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r4.claim: Asked about the passage extending through “God is kind to His servants,” ʿAlī replies, “By the Lord of the Kaʿba, the two fought,” referring to the contrasting figures in 2:204–207.
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r4.anchor: قال: سمعت عليا، في هذه الآية: " {ومن الناس من يعجبك قوله في الحياة الدنيا} [البقرة: 204] إلى

TAB-FULL:v3p588/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the adjacent verses as two opponents: one tells the other to fear God, and when the latter refuses in sinful arrogance, the first offers himself and fights him; ʿUmar praises the explanation.
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس، لبعض من كان إلى جنبه: اقتتل الرجلان. فسمع عمر، ما قال

TAB-FULL:v3p588/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r7.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r7.claim: Other interpreters specifically identify the person described with al-Akhnas b. Shurayq, as reported earlier.
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل عنى به الأخنس بن شريق

TAB-FULL:v3p588/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r8.claim: Al-mihād means a bed or bedding; Hell is the bed this hypocrite prepared for himself through hypocrisy, immorality, and rebellion.
TAB-FULL:v3p588/r8.anchor: وأما قوله: {ولبئس المهاد} [البقرة: 206] فإنه يعني ولبئس الفراش والوطاء

TABATABAI:2:204-206/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r1.claim: These verses classify people by hypocrisy versus sincerity in faith, whereas the preceding verses classify them by whether they seek this world or the next; the connection to the Hajj verses is clear.
TABATABAI:2:204-206/r1.anchor: تشتمل الآيات على تقسيم آخر للناس من حيث نتائج صفاتهم، كما أن الآيات السابقة

TABATABAI:2:204-207/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r5.claim: Al-ʿizza is dignity or might, and al-mihād is a bed or resting place.

TABATABAI:2:204-207/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r6.claim: The preposition bi is most naturally attached to al-ʿizza: this is dignity acquired through sin, reflecting the hypocrisy of a heart that disagrees with its tongue.
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r6.anchor: المعنى إنه إذا أمر بتقوى الله أخذته العزة الظاهرة

TABATABAI:2:204-207/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r7.claim: True dignity comes from God, as 3:26, 63:8, and 4:139 state; this man’s apparent worldly status is counterfeit dignity gained through sin, not a divine gift.
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r7.anchor: أن العزة المطلقة إنما هي من الله سبحانه كما قال تعالى تعز من تشاء وتذل من تشاء

TABATABAI:2:204-207/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r8.claim: He rejects attaching bi-l-ithm to akhadathu as either causative or causal: that would call the condition true dignity, whereas ‘dignity through sin’ marks it as false.
TABATABAI:2:204-207/r8.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن قوله { بالإثم } ليس متعلقا بقوله { أخذته }

TABRISI:2:204-205/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:204-205/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the three verses were revealed about a hypocritical pretender who outwardly displays what he inwardly opposes.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس نزلت الآيات الثلاثة في المرائي

TABRISI:2:204-205/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r13.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:2:204-205/r13.claim: A report from al-Ṣādiq also identifies the verses' referent as a particular person, without naming him here.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r13.anchor: وهو المروي عن الصادق ع إلا أنه عين المعني به

TABRISI:2:204-205/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r14.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:204-205/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the verses were revealed about the hypocrites generally.

TABRISI:2:204-205/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:204-205/r15.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:2:204-205/r15.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the referent as al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq, who displayed affection for the Prophet and Islam while concealing the opposite.
TABRISI:2:204-205/r15.anchor: وقال السدي: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق وكان يظهر الجميل بالنبي

TABRISI:2:206/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:206/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:206/r1.claim: Ittiqāʾ is seeking safety through what protects from danger; fearing God means guarding against His punishment.
TABRISI:2:206/r1.anchor: الاتقاء طلب السلامة بما يحجز عن المخافة واتقاء الله إنما هو اتقاء عذابه

TABRISI:2:206/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:206/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:206/r2.claim: Akhdh is the opposite of giving; ʿizza is strength that keeps one from humiliation.
TABRISI:2:206/r2.anchor: والأخذ ضد الإعطاء والعزة القوة التي تمتنع بها عن الذلة

TABRISI:2:206/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:206/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:206/r3.claim: Mihād is a bed or resting place; anything trodden or used as a bed has been prepared as a resting place.
TABRISI:2:206/r3.anchor: والمهاد الوطاء من كل شيء وكل شيء وطئته فقد مهدته

TABRISI:2:206/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:206/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:206/r4.claim: The hypocrite is told to stop his campaign of corruption and destruction of crops and offspring.
TABRISI:2:206/r4.anchor: وإذا قيل لهذا المنافق اتق الله فيما نهاك عنه من السعي في الأرض بالفساد

TABRISI:2:206/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:206/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:206/r5.claim: One explanation is that pride and tribal zeal drive him into sin, as something taking hold can compel or bind a person.
TABRISI:2:206/r5.anchor: حملته العزة وحمية الجاهلية على فعل الإثم ودعته إليه

TABRISI:2:206/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:206/r6.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:206/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains that pride seized him because of the unbelief already in his heart.
TABRISI:2:206/r6.anchor: أخذته العزة من أجل الإثم الذي في قلبه من الكفر عن الحسن

TABRISI:2:206/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:206/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:206/r7.claim: Hell is a sufficient punishment for his leading others astray.
TABRISI:2:206/r7.anchor: فكفاه عقوبة من إضلاله أن يصلى نار جهنم

TABRISI:2:206/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:206/r8.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:206/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses mihād as a settled abode; a resting place suggests permanence beneath its occupant.
TABRISI:2:206/r8.anchor: أي القرار عن الحسن كما قال في موضع آخر وبئس القرار

TABRISI:2:206/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:206/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:206/r9.claim: Another explanation calls Hell a mihād by substitution for the promised resting place, paralleling the reversed glad tidings in 31:7.
TABRISI:2:206/r9.anchor: وقيل إنما سميت جهنم مهادا لأنها بدل من المهاد كما قال سبحانه

TABRISI:2:206/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:206/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:206/r10.claim: Arrogantly refusing truth when admonished is an enormous sin; Ibn Masʿūd says an unforgiven sin is telling a man to fear God and hearing him retort, You mind yourself.
TABRISI:2:206/r10.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن من تكبر عن قبول الحق إذا دعي إليه كان مرتكبا أعظم كبيرة

TABRISI:2:206/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:206/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
TABRISI:2:206/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says a grave unforgiven sin is for a man told to fear God to answer, You mind yourself.
TABRISI:2:206/r11.anchor: قال ابن مسعود إن من الذنوب التي لا تغفر أن يقال للرجل اتق الله

THALABI:v2p120/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p120/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
THALABI:v2p120/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak say verses through Allah's compassion to servants concern the Raji expedition: Quraysh lured six Muslims with a false conversion request, ambushed them, killed three, and captured Khubayb and Zayd.
THALABI:v2p120/r1.anchor: ابن عباس والضحاك: نزلت هذه الآيات إلى قوله والله رؤف بالعباد في سرية [الرجيع]

THALABI:v2p120/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p120/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
THALABI:v2p120/r3.claim: The same account praises Khubayb's conduct in captivity: he borrowed a razor, safely held a child while armed, refused treachery, and was miraculously given fruit in Mecca.
THALABI:v2p120/r3.anchor: ابن عباس والضحاك: نزلت هذه الآيات إلى قوله والله رؤف بالعباد في سرية [الرجيع]

THALABI:v2p121/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p121/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p121/r2.claim: The executioner's defiant killing of Khubayb after being told to fear God is identified with the warning in this verse.
THALABI:v2p121/r2.anchor: فذلك قوله وإذا قيل له اتق الله الآية. يعني سلامان

THALABI:v2p123/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p123/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p123/r9.claim: The address means fear God; pride and tribal zeal rooted in sin seize the man and drive him to sin. العزة means strength, protection, and might.
THALABI:v2p123/r9.anchor: وإذا قيل له اتق الله خف الله، تكبر أخذته العزة بالإثم أي حملته العزة وحمية الجاهلية

THALABI:v2p123/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p123/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p123/r10.claim: An alternative construal is that the pride seized him because of the sin in his heart, with the pronoun suffix standing in for a lām; Antarah's verse is cited as a parallel.
THALABI:v2p123/r10.anchor: ويقال: معناه أخذته العزة بالإثم الذي في قلبه كما قام الهاء مقام اللام كقول عنترة

THALABI:v2p123/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p123/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p123/r11.claim: Hell's punishment is sufficient for him, and the resting place is wretched.
THALABI:v2p123/r11.anchor: خشية جهنم أي كفاه عذاب جهنم

THALABI:v2p123/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p123/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v2p123/r12.claim: Ibn Masud calls it one of God's greatest sins for someone told to fear God to reply, Mind your own business.
THALABI:v2p123/r12.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: إن من أكبر الذنب عند الله أن يقال للعبد: اتق الله

THALABI:v2p124/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p124/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وعلي
THALABI:v2p124/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas pictures one man admonishing another, whose pride turns to sin; the admonisher risks himself by fighting him, and Ali said of the two, By the Lord of the Kaaba, they fought one another.
THALABI:v2p124/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: أرى هاهنا من إذا أمر بتقوى الله أخذته العزة بالإثم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r1.claim: The Messenger called al-Akhnas to answer God inwardly and outwardly; arrogance and pride drew him toward sin and injustice.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r1.anchor: فدعاه الأنفة والكبر إلى الإثم والظلم، وهو قوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r2.claim: Here al-izza means invulnerability or force.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r3.claim: Qatada says that when told to hold back, the man presses on more boldly in disobedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: إذا قيل له: مهلا مهلا ازداد إقداما على المعصية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r4.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r4.claim: The people of linguistic interpretation say the pride carried, emboldened, or adorned the sin for him; taking someone by something can mean compelling him to it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r4.anchor: قال أهل المعانى: معنى (أخذته العزة بالإثم) حملته عليه، وجرأته عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r5.claim: The sense is that pride and pre-Islamic zeal impelled him to commit sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r5.anchor: وتأويل الآية: حملته العزة وحمية الجاهلية على الفعل بالإثم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r6.claim: If bi-l-ithm attaches to akhadhat, pride seized him through the sin he earned and led him to wrongdoing and lack of humility.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r6.anchor: والجار في قوله تعالى: {بالإثم} يجوز تعلقه بالأخذ وبالعزة، فإن علقته بالأخذ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r7.claim: If bi-l-ithm attaches to al-izza, it means taking pride in sin, which distances him from what God approves.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p79/r7.anchor: وإن علقته بالعزة كان المعنى الاعتزاز بالإثم، أي: اعتز بما يؤثمه فيبعده مما يرضاه الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r1.claim: The exegetes say Hell is sufficient for him as recompense and punishment; hasbuka dirham means one dirham suffices.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: كافيه الجحيم جزاء له وعذابا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r2.speaker: امرؤ القيس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r2.claim: Imru al-Qays's verse uses hasb in the sense of sufficiency: contentment and drinking one's fill suffice as wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r2.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: وحسبك من غنى شبع وري

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r3.claim: The triliteral form is obsolete; the quadriliteral ahsabani al-shayʾ means that something sufficed me.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r3.anchor: ويقال منه في الرباعي: أحسبني الشيء، إذا كفاني

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r4.speaker: يونس وأكثر النحويين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r4.claim: Yunus and most grammarians say Jahannam is a foreign proper name for the afterlife's fire, indeclinable because of foreignness and definiteness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r4.anchor: فقال يونس وأكثر النحويين: هي اسم للنار التي يعذب الله بها في الآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r5.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r5.claim: Others say Jahannam is Arabic, named for the fire's deep bottom, and is indeclinable because it is definite and feminine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: جهنم اسم عربي، سميت نار الآخرة بها لبعد قعرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r6.speaker: قطرب عن رؤبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r6.claim: Qutrub reports that Ruʾba called a deep well a jahnam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r6.anchor: قال قطرب: حكي لنا عن رؤبة (¬4) أنه قال: ركية جهنام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r7.claim: Al-mihad is the plural of al-mahd, a place prepared for sleep; it derives from making something level, as a child's cradle or ground prepared for people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r7.anchor: والمهاد: جمع المهد. والمهد: الموضع المهيأ للنوم، ومنه: مهد الصبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r8.claim: Hell is called a bed as a fixed resting place, or because it replaces a bed for them, like the substitution in the cited phrase about glad tidings of painful punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p80/r8.anchor: الثبوت عليه، وقيل: لأنها بدل من المهاد لهم

QASHANI:2:206-208/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:206-208/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:206-208/r1.claim: Egoistic zeal rooted in pre-Islamic arrogance drives him stubbornly into sin, as his self asserts itself and he assumes he knows better than his adviser.
QASHANI:2:206-208/r1.anchor: حملته الحمية النفسانية حمية الجاهلية على الإثم لجاجا وأشرا لظهور نفسه

QASHANI:2:206-208/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:206-208/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:206-208/r2.claim: Jahannam is the ultimate depth and darkness of his low spiritual rank; Qashani explains its name as a deep, dark pit.
QASHANI:2:206-208/r2.anchor: فإن جهنم معناه: مهوى بعيد العمق مظلمة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r1.claim: An Arabic poetic example means that a woman's tears are meant to strike and seize the speaker's heart; knowing a paraphrase does not reveal the wording's structure or each word's force.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r1.anchor: معنى هذا البيت أنه يقول لامرأة: ما بكيت إلى لتأخذي بمجامع قلبي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r2.claim: Arabic idioms can carry meanings not recoverable from their words alone; he lists sayings about a self-contradictory excuse, an unflappable person, and a seasoned leader.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r2.anchor: مثل قولهم: (أبى الحقين العذرة) (¬4) يضرب لمن يعتذر، وظاهر حاله يكذبه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r3.claim: Qatāda explains: when told “easy, easy,” the person instead presses further into sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: إذا قيل له: مهلا مهلا (¬1)، ازداد إقداما على المعصية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r6.claim: Understanding the explanations transmitted by exegetes still requires the foundations of Arabic vocabulary and grammar to understand God's speech.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v1p413/r6.anchor: وإنما ذكرت هذه الأمثلة لتعرف أن من تأمل مصنفات المفسرين، ووقف على معاني أقوالهم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r3.claim: The admonition is a gentle warning to stop.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r3.anchor: { وإذا قيل له اتق الله } وإذا قيل له: مهلا مهلا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r4.claim: Arrogance and pre-Islamic zeal drive him to persist in sin.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r4.anchor: { أخذته العزة بالإثم } حملته الأنفة وحمية الجاهلية على الفعل بالإثم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r5.claim: Hell is sufficient punishment and a wretched resting place.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:205-206/r5.anchor: { فحسبه جهنم } كافيه الجحيم جزاء له { ولبئس المهاد } ولبئس المقر جهنم.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r17.claim: When told to fear God, pride seizes him and drives him further into sin; Hell suffices for him and is a wretched resting place.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r17.anchor: o müfside “Allah’dan kork!” denilince de {أَخَذَتْهُ ٱلْعِزَّةُ بِٱلْإِثْمِ} onu izzet-i nefsi tutar, daha ziyade günaha sokar

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r18.claim: Jahannam is the proper feminine name for the abode of punishment; Elmalılı derives it from Arabic cehnam, itself from cehm, with the sense of a foul, coarse quality and a bottomless deep well.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r18.anchor: “Cehennem”; dâr-ı azâb olan ateşin ism-i ‘alemidir ve müennestir. Arapça “cehnâm” kelimesinden me’huz, bu da “cehm”den müştaktır.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r19.claim: An alternative view treats Jahannam as an arabized foreign word from kehennam and explains its indeclinability by foreignness and proper-name status.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r19.anchor: Bunun “kehennam”dan mu‘arreb a‘cemî olduğu ve men‘-i sarfı ‘ucme ve ‘alemiyetten neş’et ettiği de söylenmiştir.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r20.claim: The verses were revealed about Ahnes ibn Sharik of Banu Thaqif, an ally of Banu Zuhra, who professed Islam and love to the Prophet, then burned a Muslim field and killed livestock after leaving.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r20.anchor: Bu âyetler, Benî Sakîf’ten Ahnes b. Şerîk hakkında nâzil olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r21.speaker: müfessirînin ekser-i muhakkikīni
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r21.claim: Most authoritative exegetes say the passage applies generally to all hypocrites who display these traits, not only its specific occasion.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r21.anchor: mazmûn-ı âyet bu gibi evsâf ile muttasıf olan münafıkların hepsine şâmil olduğunu müfessirînin ekser-i muhakkikīni tasrih etmişlerdir.

ELMALILI:2:203-207/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r22.claim: The passage teaches that people considered for positions of responsibility should be assessed by their conduct, not merely their words.
ELMALILI:2:203-207/r22.anchor: insanların dillerine bakılmayıp hâllerinin tedkīki lüzûmunu iş‘âr için nâstan üçüncü bir kısmın hisâlini göstermiştir.

QUSHAYRI:v1p100/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p100/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p100/r1.claim: The arrogant person resents admonition as unworthy of someone like himself; if mercy lets him recognize his own faults, he accepts the counsel rather than harboring resentment for years.
QUSHAYRI:v1p100/r1.anchor: ألمثلى يقال هذا ؟ ! وأنا كذا وكذا

QUSHAYRI:v1p100/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p100/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p100/r2.claim: “Hell is enough for him” includes his present alienation, inner darkness, and constricted choices, which repeatedly punish him, before transfer to the greater punishment.
QUSHAYRI:v1p100/r2.anchor: يعني ما هو فيه في الحال من الوحشة وظلمات النفس

QUSHAYRI:v1p100/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p100/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p100/r3.claim: The present lesser torment precedes the greater one, as God says that He will make people taste the nearer punishment before the greater punishment.
QUSHAYRI:v1p100/r3.anchor: ثم إنه منقول من هذا العذاب إلى العذاب الأكبر

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r2.claim: One human type speaks attractively but has evil intent and acts as a corrupter and destroyer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r2.anchor: Bunlardan biri güzel sözlü fakat kötü niyetli, bozguncu ve yıkıcıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r4.claim: Reports connect the revelation to hypocrites who appeared friendly before the Prophet and acted destructively behind his back.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r4.anchor: Bazı münafıkların Hz. Peygamber’in yanında dost gibi gözüküp arkasından yıkıcı hareketlerde bulunmaları üzerine bu âyetlerin indiği yolunda rivayetler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r5.speaker: Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r5.claim: Razi says the verses censure bad qualities rather than particular people, so anyone bearing those qualities deserves censure.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r5.anchor: Râzî’nin de belirttiği gibi Allah Teâlâ bir topluluğu, bazı kötü niteliklerini göstererek yerdiğinde, bundan o kişilerin zatını değil niteliklerini yerdiği anlamı çıkar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r6.claim: Even if the verses originally concerned one or several hypocrites in the Prophet’s time, their warning applies to everyone who adopts hypocrisy, ostentation, corruption, or destruction.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r6.anchor: bu âyetler Hz. Peygamber dönemindeki belli bir veya birkaç münafık hakkında inmiş olsa bile münafıklık, riyakârlık, bozgunculuk, tahripçilik gibi kötü huy ve davranışlar konusunda bütün insanlar için bir uyarı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r12.claim: The taqwa expression means that a believer’s deep reverence for God keeps him away from hypocritical conduct.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r12.anchor: takvâ kökünden gelen kelime aslında, “müminin Allah’a duyduğu derin saygıdan dolayı bu tür münafıkça tutum ve davranışlardan uzak durması” anlamına gelmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r13.claim: Taqwa is the most reliable virtue against hypocrisy, ostentation, discord, and corruption; reverence for God also entails respect for every proper rule.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r13.anchor: insanı münafıklık, riyakârlık, fitne ve fesatçılık gibi ahlâksızca davranışlardan alıkoyacak en güvenilir erdem takvâdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r14.claim: People must overcome pride and arrogance to attain taqwa and act honestly, because egoistic feelings prevent reflection on justified advice and drive worse conduct.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r14.anchor: gurur, kibir gibi egoist ve yıkıcı duyguları aşmaları gerektiğini göstermektedir. Zira bu tür duygular, yapılan uyarıların haklılığı üzerinde düşünüp taşınmayı engellemekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r15.claim: “Hell is enough for him” means that after this conduct he has nowhere to go except Hell.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r15.anchor: “Artık onun, cehennemi boylamaktan başka yolu kalmamıştır” anlamında, “Ona cehennem yeter” buyurulmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r16.claim: Sincerely asking what is right, considering a search for it, and assessing warnings well require freedom from pride and taking God’s command as one’s guide.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:204/r16.anchor: önce gurur, kibir vb. saptırıcı duyguların tutsaklığından kurtulup Allah’ın buyruğunu kendisine ölçü alması, rehber edinmesi gerekir

BURHAN:v1p140/r17.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p140/r17.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p140/r17.claim: ولبئس occurs twice in al-Baqara and once in al-Hajj and al-Nur; فلبئس with فـ occurs only in al-Nahl.

TUSTARI:2:206/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:2:206/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:2:206/r1.claim: “Pride seized him through sin” means partisan zeal, as in 38:2, where the phrase means zeal and discord.
TUSTARI:2:206/r1.anchor: يعني الحمية، كما قال في ص:

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r1.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r1.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi says the root sense of 'izza is strength; 'azza 'alayya means that an affair became hard on me.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r1.anchor: ذكر أبو سليمان الدمشقي : ان أصل العزة : الشدة .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r2.claim: The first Qur'anic sense is greatness or might, as in swearing by Pharaoh's might or by God's might.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r2.anchor: ذكر بعض المفسرين أن العزة في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r3.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r3.claim: The second sense is invulnerability or power, in the statement that all might belongs to God.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r3.anchor: ذكر بعض المفسرين أن العزة في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r4.claim: The third sense is haughty zeal: when told to fear God, the wrongdoer is seized by pride that draws him to sin; the disbelievers also persist in arrogance and opposition.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p434/r4.anchor: والثالث : الحمية . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#5/r1.claim: Mihād means a bed or resting place; the verb mahhada means to prepare a bed for someone, and a child's cradle derives from it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p80#5/r1.anchor: {ولبئس المهاد} أي الفراش. ومنه يقال: مهدت فلانا إذا وطأت له. ومهد الصبي منه.

SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r1.claim: The conditional clause may be a fresh statement or coordinate with yuʿjibuka; the comparable passive in Q 2:11 raises the question of what serves as its deputy subject, a matter of scholarly disagreement.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r1.anchor: هذه الجملة الشرطية تحتمل الوجهين المتقدمين في نظيرتها، أعني كونها مستأنفة أو معطوفة على " يعجبك "

SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the bāʾ as causative: pride compelled him to sin and made him commit it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r2.anchor: قوله: " بالإثم " في هذه الباء ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أن تكون للتعدية وهو قول الزمخشري

SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r3.claim: The shaykh objects that causative bāʾ normally follows an intransitive verb, as in Q 2:17 and 2:20; use with a transitive verb is rare, as in ṣakaktu al-ḥajara bi-l-ḥajar.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وباء التعدية بابها الفعل اللازم نحو: ذهب الله بنورهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r4.claim: The bāʾ may mark cause: his sin caused pride to seize him; an unattributed poem says ignorance's pride took hold of someone.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r4.anchor: الثاني: أن تكون للسببية بمعنى أن إثمه كان سببا لأخذ العزة له كما في قوله: 901 أخذته عزة من جهله

SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r5.claim: The bāʾ may mark accompaniment and function as a circumstantial phrase, describing either the pride as tainted by sin or the man as taken while committing sin.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r5.anchor: والثالث: أن تكون للمصاحبة فتكون في محل نصب على الحال، وفيها حينئذ وجهان،

SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r6.claim: The phrase uses rhetorical completion: bi-l-ithm disambiguates al-ʿizza, which can be praiseworthy (Q 63:8; 5:54), so the reader does not mistake this pride for a virtue.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206/r6.anchor: وفي قوله " العزة بالإثم " التتميم وهو نوع من علم البديع،

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r1.claim: The primary parse makes ḥasbuhu the subject and jahannam its predicate: Hell is sufficient for him.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r1.anchor: قوله: { فحسبه جهنم } " حسبه " مبتدأ و " جهنم " خبره

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r2.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also allows jahannam to be the subject of ḥasb; if ḥasb is an active participle originating as a verbal noun, its agent fills the predicate's place, strengthened by the linking fāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: " جهنم " فاعل ب " حسب " ، ثم اختلف القائل بذلك في " حسب "

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r3.claim: Another account treats ḥasb as an indeclinable verb-like particle, either past ka-fa-hum or an imperative; the author rejects this because ḥasb inflects and takes prepositions.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r3.anchor: وقيل: بل " حسب " اسم فعل، والقائل بذلك اختلف: فقيل: اسم [فعل] ماض،

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r4.claim: Ḥasb requires annexation without becoming definite; as subject it may take an extra bāʾ, as predicate it does not, and it has no dual, plural, or feminine forms even when describing those nouns.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r4.anchor: وهو من الأسماء اللازمة للإضافة، ولا يتعرف بإضافته إلى معرفة، تقول،

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r5.claim: One account says Jahannam is a foreign word arabized from Kahanām and therefore diptote for proper-name status and foreignness.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r5.anchor: فقيل: هي أعجمية وعربت، وأصلها كهنام، فمنعها من الصرف للعلمية والعجمة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r6.claim: The preferred account is Arabic: its nūn is extra, its pattern faʿnal, and it is linked to a deep well called rakiya Jahnām or to jahm, abhorrence.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: بل هي عربية الأصل، والقائلون بذلك اختلفوا في نونها: هل هي زائدة أم أصلية؟ فالصحيح أنها زائدة ووزنها " فعنل "

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r7.claim: A competing Arabic analysis makes the nūn original and the pattern faʿlal like ʿadbas, on the claim that faʿnal does not occur in Arabic.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: بل نونها أصلية ووزنها فعلل كعدبس، قال: لأن " فعنلا " مفقود في كلامهم،

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r8.claim: The author rejects the claim that faʿnal is unattested, citing ḍaghanṭ, safanj, hajnaf, and zūnak as examples of the pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r8.anchor: لكن الصحيح إثبات هذا البناء، وجاءت منه ألفاظ، قالوا: " ضغنط " من الضغاطة

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r9.claim: The cited examples also support treating the nūn in zūnak as extra, rather than treating its wāw as a root letter; its declension restriction is then tied to femininity and proper-name status.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#2/r9.anchor: وهذا كله يدل على أن النون زائدة في " زونك " وعلى هذا فامتناعها للتأنيث والعلمية.

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r1.claim: The omitted specific object of blame is Jahannam; omission is apt because al-mihād falls at the verse ending.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r1.anchor: " ولبئس المهاد " المخصوص بالذم محذوف، أي: ولبئس المهاد جهنم،

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r2.claim: The omitted object of blame is parsed as subject, with the praise/blame clause as its predicate; the author rejects alternatives that delete an entire unsupported sentence and leave the clause disconnected.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r2.anchor: وقد تقدم الكلام على " بئس " وخلاف الناس فيها. وحذف هذا المخصوص بذلك على أنه مبتدأ

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r3.claim: Al-mihād may be the plural of mahd, bedding prepared for sleep.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r3.anchor: والمهاد فيه قولان، أحدهما: أنه جمع " مهد " وهو ما يوطأ للنوم

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r4.claim: Alternatively, al-mihād is a singular name for a bed prepared for sleep.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r4.anchor: والثاني: أنه اسم مفرد، سمي به الفراش الموطأ للنوم،

SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r5.claim: Calling Hell their bed is derisive irony: it replaces the bedding they would lie on, as in an unattributed poem where painful blows serve as a greeting.
SAMIN-DURR:2:206#3/r5.anchor: وهذا من باب التهكم والاستهزاء، أي: جعلت جهنم لهم بدل مهاد يفترشونه

QIRAAT-ER:2:206:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:206:3#1/r1.speaker: vhr
QIRAAT-ER:2:206:3#1/r1.claim: A ḍamma-kasra blend on qāf contrasts with pure kasra; both readings are canonical, and the blend preserves an archaic pronunciation without semantic difference.
QIRAAT-ER:2:206:3#1/r1.anchor: Vowel shift on qāf: ḍamma-kasra blend (qᵘīla) vs pure kasra (qīla); ishbāʿ al-ḍamma

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r11.claim: Jahannam is the proper name of Hell or its lowest level; the Arabic account derives it from a deep-bottomed well and from harshness, with an extra nūn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r11.anchor: جهنم: علم للنار وقيل: اسم الدرك الأسفل فيها، وهي عربية مشتقة من قولهم:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r12.claim: On the Arabic derivation, Jahannam is indeclinable because it is a feminine proper name, and its pattern is faʿnal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r12.anchor: وكلاهما من الجهم وهو الكراهة والغلظة، فالنون على هذا زائدة، فوزنه: فعنل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r14.claim: Some grammarians deny that faʿnal occurs in Arabic and analyze dūnka as fuʿlala, but he rejects that restriction and affirms the pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r14.anchor: والواو أصل في بنات الأربعة كهي في: ورنتل، والصحيح إثبات هذا البناء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r15.claim: He supports faʿnal with ḍaghanṭ, safanj, hajanْf, and zawna(k); zawna(k) names a short person who struts, and Hassan’s verse uses zawk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p316/r15.anchor: هجنف: للظليم والزونك: القصير سمي بذلك لأنه يزوك في مشيته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r1.claim: The cited Arabic analysis treats the nūn in Jahannam as extra and makes it indeclinable for being a feminine proper name.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r1.anchor: وهذا كله يدل على زيادة النون في: جهنم وامتنعت الصرف للعلمية والتأنيث،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r2.claim: Another etymology treats Jahannam as foreign, from Kehnam, Arabized by changing kāf to jīm and dropping the alif; it is then indeclinable for foreignness and proper-name status.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r2.anchor: وقيل: هي أعجمية وأصلها كهنام، فعربت بإبدال من الكاف جيما.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r3.claim: Ḥasb means sufficient; aḥsabani means “it sufficed me,” and ḥasb functions in place of maḥsib.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r3.anchor: حسب: بمعنى: كاف، تقول أحسبني الشيء: كفاني،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r4.claim: As a subject, ḥasb takes a predicate with an extra bāʾ; as predicate it has no bāʾ, and as an adjective it is annexed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r4.anchor: ويستعمل مبتدأ فيجر خبره بباء زائدة، وإذا استعمل خبرا لا يزاد فيه الباء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r5.claim: When annexed to a definite, ḥasb remains indefinite; it can take a specification and does not inflect for number or gender because it is a verbal noun.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r5.anchor: ولا يتعرف إذا أضيف إلى معرفة، تقول: مررت برجل حسبك، ويجيء معه التمييز نحو:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r6.claim: Al-mihād means a bed or a place prepared for sleep; another view makes it the plural of mahd.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p317/r6.anchor: المهاد: الفراش وهو ما وطئ للنوم، وقيل: هو جمع مهد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r10.claim: The sentence may be independent or included in the relative clause; Abu Hayyan points back to the analogous construction in 2:11.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r10.anchor: وإذا قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة بالإثم تحتمل أيضا هذه الجملة أن تكون مستأنفة، وتحتمل أن تكون داخلة في الصلة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r11.claim: أخذته العزة means that pride enveloped and surrounded him, as if he were a thing grasped by a hand.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p331/r11.anchor: و: أخذته العزة، احتوت عليه وأحاطت به، وصار كالمأخوذ لها كما يأخذ الشيء باليد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that his pride and pre-Islamic zeal force him into the forbidden sin, keeping him in it stubbornly and making him reject the admonisher's words.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: من قولك أخذته بكذا إذا حملته عليه، وألزمته إياه، أي: حملته العزة التي فيه، وحمية الجاهلية، على الإثم الذي ينهى عنه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r2.claim: On al-Zamakhshari's analysis, باء is causative or transitive, although this is usual with an intransitive verb and rare with an already transitive one, as in 2:20.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r2.anchor: فالباء، على كلامه للتعدية، كأن المعنى ألزمته العزة الإثم، والتعدية بالباء بابها الفعل اللازم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r3.claim: The باء may instead mean accompaniment: he is taken while accompanied by sin, or the pride itself is accompanied by sin, as a circumstantial phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r3.anchor: ويحتمل الباء أن تكون للمصاحبة، أي: أخذته مصحوبا بالإثم، أو مصحوبة بالإثم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r4.claim: Hasan takes باء as causal: prior sin, namely disbelief in the heart, causes the pride that prevents him from accepting an order to fear God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r4.anchor: وعلى أن تكون: الباء، سببية فسره الحسن، قال. أي من أجل الإثم الذي في قلبه، يعني الكفر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r5.claim: العزة is glossed as strength, zeal, or protective self-regard; these senses are close.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r5.anchor: وقد فسرت العزة بالقوة وبالحمية والمنعة، وكلها متقاربة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r6.claim: The phrase uses the rhetorical device tatmim: adding بالإثم clarifies that the pride is blameworthy, since pride may also be praised as obedience; compare 5:54, 63:8, and 4:139.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r6.anchor: وفي قوله: أخذته العزة بالإثم نوع من البديع يسمى التتميم، وهو إرداف الكلام بكلمة يرفع عنه اللبس، وتقربه للفهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r7.claim: Ibn Masud says a man should not become angry when told to fear God or respond, Who are you to say this to someone like me?
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r7.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: لا ينبغي للرجل أن يغضب إذا قيل له اتق الله، أو تقول: أو لمثلي يقال هذا؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r8.speaker: عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r8.claim: When told to fear God, Umar humbled himself by putting his cheek on the ground or prostrating, saying that was within his power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r8.anchor: وقيل لعمر: اتق الله، فوضع خده على الأرض تواضعا، وقيل: سجد، وقال: هذا مقدرتي.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r9.speaker: هارون الرشيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r9.claim: A Jew who had sought help from Harun al-Rashid for a year finally told him to fear God; Harun dismounted, prostrated, and granted the request. The excerpt breaks off just as the explanation is introduced.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p332/r9.anchor: وتردد يهودي إلى باب هارون الرشيد، سنة فلم يقض له حاجة، فتحيل حتى وقف بين يديه، فقال: اتق الله يا أمير المؤمنين:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r1.claim: The preceding warning to fear God is recalled as the context for the man’s fate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r1.anchor: قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة بالإثم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r2.claim: Hell alone suffices as his recompense and humiliation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r2.anchor: كافيه جزاء وإذلالا جهنم، وهي جملة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r3.claim: Some analyze Jahannam as the subject of بحسبه, treating حسب as a past-tense or imperative noun of action.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r4.claim: The author rejects the اسم فعل analysis because حسب takes a preposition, functions adjectivally, and inflects for case.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r4.anchor: حركات الإعراب عليه يبطل كونه اسم فعل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r5.claim: His worldly pride is answered by the punishment of Hell, the ultimate humiliation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r5.anchor: وقوبل على اعتزازه بعذاب جهنم، وهو الغاية في الذل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r6.claim: The punishment he was ordered to fear has now befallen him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r6.anchor: ما أمر أن يتقيه، وهو: عذاب الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r7.claim: The phrase magnifies the punishment, like telling someone that what befell him is more than enough.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r7.anchor: فحسبه جهنم، استعظام لما حل به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r8.claim: Following Basran grammar and Sibawayh, نعم and بئس are frozen verbs; the raised noun is their subject, and the مخصوص is a topic whether before or after.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r9.claim: The omitted object of blame is understood from context as Hell, estimated as ولبئس المهاد جهنم or هي.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r9.anchor: وحذف هنا المخصوص بالذم للعلم به إذ هو متقدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r10.claim: He rejects analyses making a delayed مخصوص a predicate of an omitted topic or a topic with omitted predicate: deletion would leave a disconnected clause without a syntactic role.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r10.anchor: من غير أن ينوب عنها شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r11.claim: Treating the omitted مخصوص as a single word leaves one clause, with no difference in structure whether it precedes or follows بئس.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r11.anchor: كما لا تجد فرقا بين: زيد قام أبوه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r12.claim: Omitting the object of blame suits the verse ending on المهاد; the Quran often omits it for this cadence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p333/r12.anchor: وحسن حذف المخصوص بالذم هنا كون المهاد وقع فاصلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r4.claim: His intense hypocrisy makes pride and anger seize him when told to fear God; because the anger is for worldly motives rather than God, it is accompanied by sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r4.anchor: استولت عليه الأنفة والغضب بالإثم. أي: مصحوبا بالإثم فليس غضبه لله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r5.claim: His outcome is Hell, sufficient for him and replacing his pride with humiliation; the author condemns this resting place as a vile end.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p358/r5.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى ما يؤول إليه حال هذا الآنف المغتر بغير الله، وهو جهنم، فهي كافية له

ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r1.claim: When told to fear God in his conduct, the man is overtaken and surrounded by pride; العزة originally opposes humiliation and here figuratively denotes haughtiness and zeal.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r1.anchor: وإذا قيل له أتق الله في فعلك أخذته العزة أي أحتوت عليه وأحاطت به

ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r2.claim: بالإثم can mean accompanied by sin or because of his prior sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r2.anchor: أي مصحوبا أو مصحوبة به أو بسبب إثمه السابق

ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r3.claim: A further derivation takes أخذ as capture: pride and pre-Islamic zeal make him a captive shackled by sin.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r4.claim: The primary parsing makes جهنم the predicate and حسبه the subject, meaning Hell suffices him.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r4.anchor: جهنم ) مبتدأ وخبر أى كافيه ( جهنم )

ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r5.claim: Another parsing makes جهنم the subject filling حسبه’s predicate position and treats حسب as an active participle; another takes حسب as a past particle meaning suffice, which Alusi questions.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r5.anchor: فاعل ل ( حسبه ) ساد مسد خبره

ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r6.claim: Jahannam is either the proper name of the punishment abode or of one of its levels, and is indeclinable because it is feminine proper name, on one analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r6.anchor: علم لدار العقاب أو لطبقة من طبقاتها ممنوعة من الصرف للعلمية والتأنيث

ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r7.claim: Al-Baḥr derives the name from a deep well, جهنام, and traces both to جهم, meaning aversion or harshness; Alusi rejects the proposed فعنلل pattern.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r7.anchor: وفي البحر إنها مشتقة من قولهم : ركية جهنام - إذا كانت بعيدة القعر وكلاهما من الجهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r8.claim: Another view derives the word from Persian كهنام, Arabized by changing kāf to jīm and dropping alif; foreignness and proper naming then explain its indeclinability.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r8.anchor: وقيل : إنها فارسى وأصلها كهنام فعربت - بإبدال الكاف جيما وإسقاط الألف -

ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r9.claim: The phrase answers an implied oath; its omitted object of blame is obvious, and المهاد means bedding or what is prepared for the side, used mockingly.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r10.claim: Scholars distinguish a litigant’s rebuke to a judge: saying “be just” or similar may warrant discretionary punishment, but saying “fear God” does not.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r10.anchor: ولهذا قال العلماء : إذا قال الخصم للقاضي : اعدل ونحوه له أن يعزره

ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says one of the gravest sins is telling a brother to fear God and hearing him answer, “Mind yourself.”
ALUSI-FULL:v2p96/r11.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه ' إتن من أكبر الذنب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r1.anchor: قوله {وإذا قيل له اتق الله} أي خف الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r2.claim: Pride and جاهلية zeal drive him to sin, meaning injustice; ʿizza here is arrogance and power or protection.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r2.anchor: أي حملته العزة وحمية الجاهلية على الفعل بالإثم أي بالظلم، والعزة: التكبر والمنعة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r3.claim: An alternative parses it as pride taking hold of him because of the sin in his heart, with the preposition bāʾ standing for lām.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r3.anchor: وقيل معناه {أخذته العزة} للإثم الذي في قلبه، فأقام الباء مقام اللام.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r4.claim: Jahannam is sufficient for him; al-mahād means a bed or resting place.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r4.anchor: {فحسبه جهنم} أي كافيه {ولبئس المهاد} أي الفراش

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masud says one of the greatest sins before God is for a servant told to fear God to answer, “Mind yourself.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r5.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: إن من أكبر الذنب عند الله أن يقال: للعبد اتق الله فيقول: عليك بنفسك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r6.claim: When Umar ibn al-Khattab was told to fear God, he put his cheek on the ground in humility before God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p236#2/r6.anchor: وروي أنه قيل لعمر بن الخطاب: اتق الله، فوضع خده على الأرض تواضعا لله عز وجل.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p237/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p237/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p237/r1.claim: Umar marveled that God protected Asim after death because Asim had vowed that no polytheist would touch him and that he would not touch one; God protected him after death just as in life.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p237/r1.anchor: وكان عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يقول حين بلغه أن الدبر منعته يقول:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p237/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p237/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p237/r4.claim: The verse is applied to the polytheist Salamān, who thrust a spear through Khubayb after Khubayb told him to fear God; the warning only made him more obstinate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p237/r4.anchor: وذلك قوله عز وجل {وإذا قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة بالإثم} يعني سلامان

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r1.claim: Arrogance and jāhiliyya zeal drive him stubbornly into the very sin he is told to avoid; “took him with” means compelled and bound him to it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r1.anchor: حملته الأنفة وحمية الجاهلية على الإثم الذي يؤمر باتقانه لجاجا، من قولك أخذته بكذا إذا حملته عليه وألزمته إياه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r2.claim: Hell suffices him as recompense and punishment; Jahannam is the proper name of the abode of punishment, originally synonymous with fire, or a loanword.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r2.anchor: كفته جزاء وعذابا، و { جهنم } علم لدار العقاب

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r3.claim: This is the answer to an implied oath; the condemned subject is omitted because it is understood.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r3.anchor: جواب قسم مقدر والمخصوص بالذم محذوف للعلم به

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r4.claim: Al-mihād means a bed, or that which is spread beneath someone lying down.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:206/r4.anchor: والمهاد الفراش. وقيل ما يوطأ للجنب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r15.claim: His response to admonition distinguishes him from people who stop when corrected, confirming his extreme contentiousness.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r15.anchor: ولما كان من الناس من يفعل الفساد فإذا نهى عنه انتهى بين أن هذا على غير ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r16.claim: Anyone may warn him to leave corruption out of fear of God, under whose power everything lies.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r16.anchor: أي الملك الأعظم الذي كل شيء تحت قهره واترك ما أنت عليه من الفساد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r17.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r17.claim: Arrogance takes hold through ingrained pride and contempt for God's command; such pride is not proper to creatures.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r17.anchor: في نفسه لما فيها من الكبرياء والاستهانة بأمر الله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r18.claim: True might belongs to God alone, as the author recalls with the phrase that all might belongs to God.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r18.anchor: وليس من شأن الخلق الاتصاف بذلك فإن العزة لله جميعا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r19.claim: He is seized by arrogance while sinning: base conduct that violates what is lawful and includes contempt and haughtiness toward others.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p384/r19.anchor: أي مصاحبا للذنب , وهو العمل الرذل السافل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r1.claim: Hell is punishment enough for him and becomes his bed, matching the way he prepared himself to pursue corruption.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r1.anchor: تكون مهادا له كما مهد للفساد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r2.claim: Jahannam suggests a grim face-to-face reception, fitting his confrontation of the person who admonished him.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r2.anchor: وتخصيص هذا الاسم المنبئ عن الجهامة في المواجهة أي الاستقبال بوجه كريه لما وقع منه من المواجهة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r3.claim: Al-Harali says God uses a particular name for the Fire when it conveys a meaning relevant to the judgment.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r3.anchor: قال الحرالي : فلمعنى ما يختص بالحكم يسمي تعالى النار باسم من أسمائها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r4.claim: Al-Harali defines mihād as a place of rest or a comfortable, prepared thing that is spread and trodden.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r4.anchor: والمهاد موطن الهدوء والمستطاب مما يستفرش ويوطأ

BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r5.claim: Al-Harali sees the verse as respite for this community out of regard for its Prophet: evildoers and disbelievers face the afterlife, with a long stay and eternity there.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r5.anchor: فيه إشعار بإمهال الله عز وجل لهذه الأمة رعاية لنبيها فأحسب فاجرها وكافرها بعذاب الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r6.claim: Al-Harali adds that hastening worldly punishment for believers would leave disbelievers worldly life while believers receive the next life.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p385/r6.anchor: ولو عاجل مؤمنها بعقوبة الدينا فخلص لكافرها الدنيا ولمؤمنها الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v1p574/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿud says it is a grave sin for a man told by his brother to fear God to respond by telling him to mind his own business.
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r9.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: إن من أكبر الذنب عند الله أن يقول الرجل

DURR-FULL:v1p574/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r10.speaker: سفيان
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r10.claim: Sufyan reports that when a man told Malik ibn Mughawil to fear God, Malik placed his cheek on the ground in humility before God.
DURR-FULL:v1p574/r10.anchor: عن سفيان قال: قال رجل لمالك بن مغول: اتق الله فقط

DURR-FULL:v1p575/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p575/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p575/r1.claim: A man admonished ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab to fear God; ʿUmar said there is no good in us if others do not admonish us, nor in them if they do not speak up.
DURR-FULL:v1p575/r1.anchor: عن الحسن أن رجلا قال لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه: اتق الله

DURR-FULL:v1p575/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p575/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p575/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the wretched resting place as what its inhabitants prepared for themselves.
DURR-FULL:v1p575/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ولبئس المهاد} قال: بئس ما مهدوا لأنفسهم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p368/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p368/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNABIHATIM:v2p368/r1.claim: ʿAlī recited through the next verse and said, 'These two have fought,' linking the groups in 2:206–207.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p368/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p368/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p368/r2.claim: Mujāhid explains the evil resting place as what they prepared for themselves.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p368/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد في قول الله : ولبئس المهاد قال : بئس ما مهدوا لانفسهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r1.claim: When an admonisher reminds him of what entails mindfulness of God, he becomes angry at the admonition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r1.anchor: أي وإذا وعظه واعظ بما يقتضي تذكيره بتقوى الله تعالى غضب لذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r2.claim: أخذ originally means taking by hand, then commonly means taking control, overpowering, receiving, or enveloping; here جاهلية pride has enveloped him. The cited Quranic uses include 9:5, 6:42, and 3:81.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r2.anchor: والأخذ أصله تناول الشيء باليد ، واستعمل مجازا مشهورا في الاستيلاء قال تعالى : { وخذوهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r3.claim: العزة is the holder’s belief that no one can overpower him or challenge his speech, based on his standing among his people and their strength; Samawʾal’s verse illustrates their inability to contradict his group.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r3.anchor: والعزة صفة يرى صاحبها أنه لا يقدر عليه غيره ولا يعارض في كلامه لأجل مكانته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r4.claim: The word also means strength and dominance, often grounded in tribal numbers among Arabs, though bravery can replace numbers; the proverb and Samawʾal’s verse illustrate this, and the adjective appears at 2:209.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r4.anchor: ومنه العزة بمعنى القوة والغلبة وإنما تكون غالبا في العرب بسبب كثرة القبيلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r5.claim: The definite article in العزة is referential: it denotes familiar pre-Islamic pride that bars its owner from accepting blame or correction; being seized by it implies refusing counsel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271/r5.anchor: ف ( أل ) في ( العزة ) للعهد أي العزة المعروفة لأهل الجاهلية التي تمنع صاحبها من قبول اللوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r1.claim: The bāʾ marks accompaniment: sinful, unjust pride. This qualification distinguishes it from the praiseworthy pride affirmed at 63:8; it blocks admonition and leaves him attached to habitual sin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r1.anchor: وقوله : { بالإثم } الباء فيه للمصاحبة أي أخذته العزة الملابسة للإثم والظلم وهو احتراس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r2.claim: The threat follows from that state. Since حسب means sufficiency and what suffices is normally fit for someone, he uses it for recompense; Abu al-Ṭayyib’s line illustrates fitting measure.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r2.anchor: وأصل الحسب هو الكافي كما سيجيء عند قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r3.claim: Jahannam is a proper name for the punishment abode and is indeclinable; some grammarians explain this by definiteness and femininity, while most explain it by definiteness and foreign origin, making etymological inquiry unnecessary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r3.anchor: وجهنم علم على دار العقاب الموقدة نارا ، وهو اسم ممنوع من الصرف قال بعض النحاة للعلمية والتأنيث

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r4.claim: Some derive the name from Arabic جهم, ‘abhorrence,’ proposing patterns with doubled nūn or a repeated nūn; the author answers that rare patterns are attested in دونك and حفنكى.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r4.anchor: ومن جعله عربيا زعم أنه مشتق من الجهم وهو الكراهية فزعم بعضهم أن وزنه فعنل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r5.claim: Other derivations say the name was borrowed and Arabized from Persian كهنام or Hebrew كهنام.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r5.anchor: ومن قال : أصلها بالفارسية كهنام فعربت جهنم . وقيل أصلها عبرانية كهنام بكسر الكاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r6.claim: Calling a deep well ركية جهنم does not prove an Arabic derivation: the well is likened to Hell as an immensely deep, fire-filled pit.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r6.anchor: وأما قول العرب ركية جهنم أي بعيدة القعر فلا حجة فيه ، لأنه ناشىء عن تشبيه الركية بجهنم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r7.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل أو أمية بن أبي الصلت
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r7.claim: A poem attributed uncertainly to Waraqa ibn Nawfal or Umayya ibn Abi al-Ṣalt, lamenting Zayd ibn ʿAmr, depicts Hell as a dark, fiery oven; the passage links this image to 2:24 and says hadith likewise describes it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p271#2/r7.anchor: قال ورقة بن نوفل أو أمية بن أبي الصلت يرثي زيدا بن عمرو بن نفيل وكانا معا ممن ترك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p272/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p272/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p272/r1.claim: The hadith likewise depicts Hell as a fiery oven; the Quran names it fire in many places and says people and stones fuel it, as discussed at 2:24.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p272/r1.anchor: وقد جاء وصف جهنم في الحديث بمثل ذلك وسماها الله في كتابه في مواضع كثيرة نارا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p272/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p272/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p272/r2.claim: مهاد is what is prepared for sleeping; calling Hell a bed is mockery because sinners are thrown into it and their sides and backs meet it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p272/r2.anchor: والمهاد ما يمهد أي يهيأ لمن ينام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p273/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p273/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p273/r6.claim: The passage teaches believers to discern inner realities and not be deceived by appearances before testing: a person may speak sweetly and look good while concealing evil and plotting harm.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r1.claim: This describes an arrogant unbeliever or hypocrite, full of self-importance; a believer should avoid putting another person under such pressure.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r1.anchor: هذه صفة الكافر أو المنافق الذاهب بنفسه زهوا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r2.claim: Some scholars say it is enough of a sin to answer a brother’s admonition, “mind yourself; someone like you advises me?”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r2.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: كفى بالمرء إثما أن يقول له أخوه اتق الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r3.claim: Al-ʿizza means invulnerability and force of spirit: pride seizes him and carries him into sin.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r4.claim: Alternatively, pride seized him together with sin; bā has a different function on the two readings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r4.anchor: ويحتمل لفظ الآية أن يكون أخذته العزة مع الإثم، فمعنى الباء يختلف بحسب التأويلين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r5.claim: Hasbuhu means that Hell is sufficient as punishment and recompense.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r6.claim: Al-mihād is bedding a person prepares for himself, like a mattress; a poetic line equates greeting with a painful blow.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r6.anchor: والمهاد ما مهد الرجل لنفسه كأنه الفراش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r8.claim: The preceding verses appear to concern unbelievers generally; sinners sharing these traits also incur a portion of the warning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p281/r8.anchor: والظاهر من هذا التقسيم أن تكون الآيات قبل هذا على العموم في الكافر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r9.claim: The report says this verse and the next three were revealed concerning al-Zubayr, al-Miqdad, Khubayb and the other expedition members, as well as the hypocrites.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p220/r9.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى في الزبير والمقداد وخبيب وأصحابه والمنافقين هذه الآية وثلاث آيات بعدها وهذا الحديث بطوله مروي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains ʿizza as zealotry; a poem is cited for the phrase “zealotry took him.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس هي الحمية وأنشدوا أخذته عزة من جهله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r2.claim: The sense is that his pride or zealotry drives him to commit sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r2.anchor: ومعنى الكلام حملته الحمية على الفعل بالإثم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r3.claim: One analysis by Ibn al-Anbari treats Jahannam as a foreign word, indeclinable here because it is definite and foreign.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r3.anchor: وفي جهنم قولان ذكرهما ابن الأنباري أحدهما أنها أعجمية لا تجر للتعريف والعجمة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari's second analysis treats Jahannam as Arabic and indeclinable because it is feminine and definite.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r4.anchor: والثاني أنها اسم عربي ولم يجر للتأنيث والتعريف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r5.claim: The author cites Ruʾba and al-Aʿsha using Jahannam without declension as evidence that it is an Arabicized foreign name.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r5.anchor: قال رؤبة ركبة جهنام بعيدة القعر وقال الأعشى دعوت خليلي مسحلا ودعوا له جهنام جدعا للهجين المذمم فترك صرفه يدل على أنه اسم أعجمي معرب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r6.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r6.claim: One interpretation is that Hell is sufficient punishment for his sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r6.anchor: وفي المعنى الكلام قولان أحدها فحسبه جهنم جزاء عن إثمه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r7.claim: Another interpretation is that Hell is sufficient humiliation in response to his pride.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r7.anchor: والثاني فحسبه جهنم ذلا من عزة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r8.claim: Al-mihad means a bed or resting place.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r8.anchor: والمهاد الفراش ومهدت لفلان إذا وطأت له

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r9.claim: The same root is used for preparing a place for someone and for a child's cradle.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p222#2/r9.anchor: ومهدت لفلان إذا وطأت له ومنه مهد الصبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564#2/r1.claim: When the wicked man is urged to fear God, abandon sinful speech and deeds, and return to truth, pride and anger overtake him and he refuses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564#2/r1.anchor: إذا وعظ هذا الفاجر في مقاله وفعاله، وقيل له: اتق الله، وانزع عن قولك وفعلك، وارجع إلى الحق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564#2/r2.claim: The verse resembles 22:72, where disbelievers react with anger when clear revelations are recited to them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564#2/r2.anchor: وهذه الآية شبيهة بقوله تعالى: {وإذا تتلى عليهم آياتنا بينات تعرف في وجوه الذين كفروا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564#2/r3.claim: Hell is punishment enough for him, and it is an evil resting place.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p564#2/r3.anchor: أي: هي كافيته عقوبة في ذلك

JISHUMI:v1p837/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p837/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p837/r2.claim: Mihād means a surface or bed beneath something.

JISHUMI:v1p837/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p837/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p837/r3.claim: Taking is the opposite of giving.

JISHUMI:v1p837/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p837/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p837/r4.claim: ʿIzza is the strength by which a person avoids humiliation.
JISHUMI:v1p837/r4.anchor: والعزة: القوة التي يمتنع بها من الذلة

JISHUMI:v1p837/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p837/r5.speaker: السدي
JISHUMI:v1p837/r5.claim: Al-Suddi reports that the verse was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Shariq al-Thaqafi.
JISHUMI:v1p837/r5.anchor: قيل: نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق الثقفي، عن السدي

JISHUMI:v1p837/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p837/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p837/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the verse concerns hypocrites generally.
JISHUMI:v1p837/r6.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في كل منافق، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p837/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p837/r7.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v1p837/r7.claim: Al-Asamm explains the admonition as fear God, avoid disobeying Him, fear His punishment, or make one's inward state match one's outward state.
JISHUMI:v1p837/r7.anchor: وقيل: اتق الله واجعل باطنك كظاهرك، عن الأصم

JISHUMI:v1p838/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p838/r1.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p838/r1.claim: Another explanation treats Hell as an appositive for al-mihād, so Hell is called by the same name.

JISHUMI:v1p838/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p838/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p838/r2.claim: Human acts belong to human agents: otherwise rebuking the person, describing his pride in sin, condemning him, and threatening punishment would make no sense.
JISHUMI:v1p838/r2.anchor: الآية تدل على أن أفعال العباد فعلهم

JISHUMI:v1p838/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p838/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p838/r3.claim: A person who arrogantly refuses to accept the truth when summoned to it commits a major sin.
JISHUMI:v1p838/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن من دعي إلى حق فتكبر عن قبوله كان ذلك كبيرة منه

JISHUMI:v1p838/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p838/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p838/r4.claim: This conduct amounts to audacity toward God and approaches unbelief.
JISHUMI:v1p838/r4.anchor: وتدل على أن هذا النوع من الصنيع يجري مجرى التجرؤ على الله، فيقرب من الكفر

JISHUMI:v1p838/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p838/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p838/r5.claim: The wording that Hell suffices him indicates there is no punishment beyond Hellfire.
JISHUMI:v1p838/r5.anchor: وتدل على أنه لا عذاب وراء عذاب جهنم، لذلك قال: فحسبه جهنم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p279/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p279/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p279/r1.claim: The construction “he was seized by X” means X drove him; pride and pre-Islamic zeal force him into the forbidden sin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p279/r1.anchor: من قولك أخذته بكذا إذا حملته عليه وألزمته اياه أي حملته العزة التي فيه وحمية الجاهلية على الإثم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p279/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p279/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p279/r2.claim: His obstinacy makes him persist either to cause harm or out of stubbornness, or to reject the preacher’s admonition.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p279/r2.anchor: والزمته ارتكابه وان لا يخلى عنه ضرارا ولجاجا أو على رد قول الواعظ

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r27.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r27.claim: One explanation is that pride drives him to commit sin.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r27.anchor: أحدهما : معناه دعته العزة إلى فعل الإثم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r28.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r28.claim: Alternatively, because of his sin, pride prevents him from accepting the admonition to fear God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p264/r28.anchor: والثاني : معناه إذا قيل له اتق الله , عزت نفسه أن يقبلها , للإثم الذي منعه منها .

MUQATIL:2:204-206/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r7.claim: “Pride seizes him through sin” means zeal; 38:2’s reference to pride and dissension likewise means sinful zeal.
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r7.anchor:
نظيرها فى ص [آية: 2] قوله سبحانه:
بل الذين كفروا في عزة وشقاق

MUQATIL:2:204-206/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r8.claim: Hell, with its severe punishment, is enough for him, and it is a wretched resting place.
MUQATIL:2:204-206/r8.anchor: فحسبه جهنم } شدة عذاب، { ولبئس المهاد }

NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r1.speaker: author
