NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r1.claim: The person addressed is al-Akhnas, told to fear God regarding his corruption and destruction.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r1.anchor: للأخنس ﴿ اتق الله ﴾ فى الإفساد والإهلاك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r2.claim: The expression may mean pride and pre-Islamic zeal compel him to commit the sin he is warned against, or that pride seizes him because of the unbelief in his heart.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r2.anchor: وحميّة الجاهلية على الإثم الذى ينهى عنه وألزمته ارتكابه أو الباء للسبب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r3.claim: Hell is enough for him and is the wretched resting place, like a bed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r3.anchor: أى كافيه ﴿ ولبئس المهاد ﴾ أى الفراش جهنم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r4.claim: Another occasion is Suhayb’s escape: polytheists tried to make him abandon Islam, killed companions with him, and accepted his wealth in exchange for his release and journey to Medina.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r4.anchor: ونزل فى صهيب حين أراده المشركون على ترك الإسلام وقتلوا نفرا كانوا معه فاشترى نفسه بما له منهم وأتى المدينة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r5.claim: The verse may also concern someone who enjoins right and forbids wrong until he is killed.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p100/r5.anchor: أو فيمن يأمر بالمعروف وينهى عن المنكر حتى يقتل

BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r1.claim: The person addressed is the hypocrite and corrupter, being admonished and counseled.

BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r2.claim: The admonition means to fear God in one's wrongdoing and abandon the corruption and hypocrisy one is practicing.
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r2.anchor: خف من الله في صنعك السوء واترك ما تباشره

BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r3.claim: His arrogance or pre-Islamic zeal drives him into sin, or makes him reject the preacher's advice from stubbornness; the باء marks causation, from the idiom 'he made him do X'.
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r3.anchor: حملته الأنفة التي فيها وحميته الجاهلية على الإثم

BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r4.claim: Hell and lasting entry there suffice as recompense for what he has done; this is a severe threat.
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r4.anchor: أي : كافيه دخول النار والخلود فيها

BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r5.claim: The phrase swears that Hell is a wretched bed.

BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r6.claim: Ibn Masʿūd calls it among God's greatest sins for a servant told to fear God to retort, 'Worry about yourself.'
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r6.anchor: قال ابن مسعود رضي الله تعالى عنه من أكبر الذنب

BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r7.claim: When ʿUmar was told to fear God, he put his cheek on the ground in humility.
BURSEVI:v1p265#2/r7.anchor: وقيل لعمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه اتقق الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r1.claim: This describes the conceited unbeliever or hypocrite; believers should avoid putting themselves in an embarrassing position through such conduct.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r1.anchor: هذه صفة الكافر والمنافق الذاهب بنفسه زهوا، ويكره للمؤمن أن يوقعه الحرج في بعض هذا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r2.speaker: عبد الله
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r2.claim: Abdullah says it is enough of a sin for someone to answer a brother's admonition to fear God by telling him to mind his own business.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r2.anchor: أن يقول له أخوه: اتق الله، فيقول: عليك بنفسك مثلك يوصيني!

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r3.claim: Al-ʿizza can mean strength or domination, from ʿazza yaʿizzuhu, to overcome; 38:23 uses the same root for prevailing in speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r3.anchor: والعزة: القوة والغلبة من عزه يعزه إذا غلبه. ومنه: وعزني في الخطاب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r4.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r4.claim: One view takes al-ʿizza as zeal or haughtiness, illustrated by a poet describing pride born of ignorance that makes a man turn away angrily.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r4.anchor: وقيل: العزة هنا الحمية ومنه قول الشاعر: أخذته عزة من جهله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r5.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r5.claim: Another view takes al-ʿizza as invulnerability and force of self: pride overcomes and compels him into sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r5.anchor: وقيل: العزة هنا المنعة وشدة النفس، أي اعتز في نفسه وانتحى فأوقعته تلك العزة في الإثم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r6.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r6.claim: Qatada says that when admonished to hold back, the man presses on more strongly in sin because pride drives him into it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: المعنى إذا قيل له مهلا ازداد إقداما على المعصية والمعنى حملته العزة على الإثم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r7.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r7.claim: Another explanation says he commits unbelief out of pride and pre-Islamic zeal, as in 38:2.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r7.anchor: وقيل: أخذته العزة بما يؤثمه، أي ارتكب الكفر للعزة وحمية الجاهلية. ونظيره: بل الذين كفروا في عزة وشقاق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r8.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r8.claim: Some take the bāʾ to mean li: pride prevents accepting admonition because of hypocrisy and sin in his heart; Antara's line illustrates this use of bāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r8.anchor: وقيل: الباء في «بالإثم» بمعنى اللام، أي أخذته العزة والحمية عن قبول الوعظ للإثم الذي في قلبه، وهو النفاق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r9.speaker: عنترة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r9.claim: Antara's poem about a camel illustrates the bāʾ in the sense of li, meaning that the fuel was stoked for the cauldron.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r9.anchor: ومنه قول عنترة يصف عرق الناقة: وكأن ربا أو كحيلا معقدا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r10.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r10.claim: Others take the bāʾ to mean maʿa, so pride seizes him together with sin; its sense varies with the interpretations.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r10.anchor: وقيل: الباء بمعنى مع، أي أخذته العزة مع الإثم فمعنى الباء يختلف بحسب التأويلات.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r11.speaker: هارون الرشيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r11.claim: A Jewish petitioner, kept waiting for a year, admonished Harun al-Rashid to fear God; Harun dismounted, prostrated, granted the request, and explained that the verse came to mind.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r11.anchor: وذكر أن يهوديا كانت له حاجة عند هارون الرشيد، فاختلف إلى بابه سنة، فلم يقض حاجته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r12.claim: Hasbuhu means Hell suffices as punishment and recompense, as when one tells a person that what befell him is enough to show its gravity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r12.anchor: حسبه أي كافيه معاقبة وجزاء كما تقول للرجل: كفاك ما حل بك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r13.claim: Al-mihād is the plural of mahd, a prepared sleeping place or a baby's cradle; Hell is called this as the unbelievers' settled abode.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206/r13.anchor: والمهاد جمع المهد، وهو الموضع المهيأ للنوم ومنه مهد الصبي. وسمى جهنم مهادا لأنها مستقر الكفار.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206#2/r1.claim: An alternative calls Hell a replacement for a bed, as in the warning to give glad tidings of painful punishment.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:206#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206#2/r2.claim: The expression greeting between them is a painful blow is another example of naming a painful reality with a term normally associated with welcome.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:206#2/r2.anchor: ونظيره من الكلام قولهم: تحية بينهم ضرب وجيع

RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.claim: The descriptions encourage sound conduct in hearts and limbs and remind people that God cannot be kept unaware of their inner affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v5p167#2/r2.anchor: والغرض بكل ذلك أن يبعث العباد على الطريقة الحسنة فيما يتصل بأفعال القلوب والجوارح

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r8.claim: The five traits do not prove hypocrisy: each can also characterize a show-off or another sinner; hypocrites are included, but not every person described must be one.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r8.anchor: فثبت أنا متى حملنا الآية على الموصوف بهذه الصفات الخمسة دخل فيها المنافق والمرائي

RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r13.claim: Responding to an admonition with sinful pride likewise does not necessarily indicate hypocrisy.
RAZI-FULL:v5p168/r13.anchor: وخامسها : قوله : { وإذا قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة بالإثم } فهذا أيضا لا يقتضي النفاق

RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r1.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says the Messenger called the man to abandon these acts, but pride and disdain led him to wrongdoing.
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r1.anchor: قال الواحدي : قوله تعالى : { وإذا قيل له اتق الله أخذته العزة } معناه أن رسول الله دعاه إلى ترك هذه الأفعال

RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r2.claim: Rāzī calls al-Wāḥidī's explanation weak: the verse does not say who told him to fear God or even establish that this occurred; a report would be needed, though the Prophet called everyone to piety.

RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r3.claim: The command to fear God applies to all five faults: worldly ambition, false oaths, obstinate defense of falsehood, corruption, and destruction of crops and progeny.

RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r4.claim: One idiomatic reading compares the phrase to compelling someone to do something: arrogance impels him to sin, namely ignoring and refusing to hear the admonisher.
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r4.anchor: أن هذا مأخوذ من قولهم أخذت فلانا بأن يعمل كذا

RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, arrogance has become attached to him or overtaken him, as fever does; his sinful pride arises from disbelief, ignorance, and failure to consider proofs.
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r5.anchor: أي لزمته يقال : أخذته الحمى أي لزمته

RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r6.claim: The bāʾ can mean because of or function like lām, as in saying that one acted because of someone or punished him for his offense.

RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r7.claim: The pride caused by unbelief is like the state described in 38:2, where disbelievers are in arrogance and opposition.
RAZI-FULL:v5p172#2/r7.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : { بل الذين كفروا فى عزة وشقاق }

RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r1.claim: Exegetes gloss the phrase as Hell sufficing him as recompense and punishment, as a dirham can suffice someone or God can suffice us.
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون : كافيه جهنم جزاء له وعذابا

RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r2.speaker: يونس وأكثر النحويين
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r2.claim: Yūnus and most grammarians say Jahannam is a foreign name for the fire of the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r2.anchor: جهنم فقال يونس وأكثر النحويين : هي اسم للنار

RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r3.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r3.claim: Others regard Jahannam as an Arabic name for Hell, derived from the great depth of its pit.
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون . جهنم اسم عربي سميت نار الآخرة بها

RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r4.speaker: رؤبة
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r4.claim: Ruʾba's phrase about a deep well supplies evidence for the Arabic root sense of great depth.
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r4.anchor: حكى عن رؤبة أنه قال : ركية جهنام بريد بعيدة القعر

RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r5.claim: One reading takes al-mihād and tamhīd as laying or preparing, from a bed; 51:48 calls the earth spread out and its spreaders good, and 30:44 speaks of preparing for oneself.
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r5.anchor: أن المهاد والتمهيد : التوطئة ، وأصله من المهد

RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r6.claim: A second reading makes al-mihād an evil resting place, as in the verse calling Hell an evil settlement.
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r6.anchor: أي لبئس المستقر كقوله : { جهنم يصلونها وبئس القرار }

RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r7.speaker: بعض العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r7.claim: Some scholars understand al-mihād as a sleeping bed: the person punished in Hell is laid upon its fire as his bed.
RAZI-FULL:v5p173/r7.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء : المهاد الفراش للنوم

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p310/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p310/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p310/r5.claim: The phrase may mean that sinful conduct seized him or that pride impelled him to sin or made him boast of sin.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p310/r5.anchor: فإن الجار يجوز تعلقه بشيئين، بالأخذ وبالعزة
